what: What OpenOCD 0.11 answers when the OpenOCD backend selects its probe by serial, recorded on the bench. Ubuntu 22.04 packages OpenOCD 0.11, which has no `adapter serial`: the generic selector came with 0.12, and 0.11 has one selector per adapter driver. `reset_target_run` is 0.11 refusing `adapter serial`: it prints the usage of the `adapter` group, names the words it could not place, and exits 1. `version` is its `--version`. Each `adapter_driver_*` is what `adapter name` answers once an interface script is loaded, at the configuration stage, where no adapter is opened; `adapter_driver_undefined` loaded none, and `adapter_driver_missing_script` named one that is not there. Each `selector_*` is one driver's own selector given a probe serial at the configuration stage. `probe_target_hla_serial` and `reset_target_run_hla_serial` are the product's own calls with the probe selected by `hla_serial`, on the board, and `probe_target_hla_serial_no_such_probe` is the same read selecting a serial no attached probe carries. The unit tier replays the streams byte for byte, so the selection is held to this release's own words.
how: The bench tier's test_a_real_reset_over_the_probe_is_a_success_and_carries_whatever_openocd_said, run by `tools/bench_in_container.py --distribution ubuntu-22.04` with `-vv -l`, one Nucleo-F446RE attached through its on-board debugger, agentic-hil 0.21.6.dev0 at commit 0ce1f8e. The streams are the product's own `programmer_output` for `reset_target` in mode `run`, as the tier printed the report. The runner withholds the probe serial in every line it prints; it is replaced here by the suite's synthetic serial 066BFF505050505050505050, and nothing else is changed. Every other entry was recorded on 2026-09-28 by a throwaway pytest module in tests/bench, run by `tools/bench_in_container.py --distribution ubuntu-22.04` against the same board, agentic-hil 0.21.6.dev0 at commit 94e2dfb. The module ran each `argv` through the product's own spawn in the project the tier configured, and ran `probe_target` and `reset_target` through the product's tool service with the probe selection replaced by `hla_serial <serial>`, taking OpenOCD's streams out of the log the product wrote for each call. `<scratch>` stands for the module's temporary directory, where it wrote the one-line interface scripts `adapter driver dummy` and `adapter driver remote_bitbang`. The bench's probe serial is replaced by the synthetic serial as above; `probe_target_hla_serial_no_such_probe` and the `selector_*` entries selected the synthetic serial itself, which no attached probe carries.
